title: workhorse-security: one standard for hardening and scanning every repository InStrand works in
description: Plan of record: docs/plans/2026-11-11-security-scanning-standard.md (draft v5). A thin wrapper around tools other people maintain, adding only what they leave open for InStrand's stacks and customers, and improving from its own findings. Six parts: repository config, surface, check, fragment, canary, record. Every capability is a combination of them. One child epic per wave of section 12.

title: Ryan: confirm or veto the decisions of 11 November (D9 to D13) and the mission in AGENTS.md
description: Standard section 13. D9: public or private (created private under InStrand; recommendation: public, because a consumer's CI cannot check out a private pack without a credential and the gate cannot be called from a customer organisation). D10: the pack's code is dependency-free Node, not bash plus jq. D11: the gate stops only what a change adds, reads exceptions from the base revision, and switches off scanners' own ignore mechanisms. D12: data paths apply only to checks that send content to a provider; local checks scan everything. D13: directory names. Also open from before: D2 (Renovate), D3 (whose API key for the CI reviewer), D8 (cadence and fix-time targets). The mission region in AGENTS.md is marked proposed. Acceptance: each decision recorded here as confirmed, amended or vetoed, and the standard updated.
close_reason: Answered by Ryan on 11 November 2026. D9: public. D10 to D13 and the mission: confirmed under his delegation ('they generally sound fine'). D14 added from his direction on where the audit skill lives. D2, D3 and D8 stay open on their own beads. Recorded in standard section 13.

title: Wave 0: bootstrap (11 November 2026)
description: Standard section 12, wave 0. The repository, the runner, the gate with three pinned checks, the starter rules and canaries, the fragments, the audit skill in its first form. Complete when CI is green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Wave 0 complete: every child closed with evidence; CI green on both runners.

title: Repository scaffold: AGENTS.md, README, licence, ignores, pre-push hook with the confidentiality check, dev setup, CI workflows
description: Modelled on flywheel-teams. Acceptance: test/prepush-gate.test.sh passes (a push with a listed term is refused; the tests run from a git archive of the pushed commit); shellcheck clean.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: test/prepush-gate.test.sh passes locally and in CI run 42951014283; the first push went through the hook.

title: The whs runner: check registry, pinned install, surfaces, scan, gate, findings identity and comparison
description: lib/*.mjs and checks/registry.json. Acceptance: test/unit.test.mjs and test/gate.test.mjs pass, including the planted negatives: a change that excuses itself from the head revision, a change that hides itself with a scanner ignore file or inline comment, a secret added and removed inside the change, and a scanner that errors.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: test/unit.test.mjs and test/gate.test.mjs pass (27 Node tests in all) locally, in the pre-push hook and in CI run 42951014283 on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest. The self-excuse and self-hide negatives failed first and found a real defect, now fixed.

title: Three starter Semgrep rules and ten canaries; the canary suite fails when proof is missing
description: Rules: SECURITY DEFINER without search_path; a privilege granted to the anonymous role; a command, server or permission allow entry in agent configuration. Canaries for gitleaks, zizmor and Semgrep with a catching and a quiet case each. Acceptance: node bin/whs.mjs canary reports 10 cases, 0 failures; test/canary.test.mjs plants five defects and each is reported.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: whs canary 10 cases, 0 failures; test/canary.test.mjs plants five defects and each is reported.

title: Coverage modes (Ryan, 11 Nov): run without the jsm skills and say so
description: The mode is derived, not switched: fragments/registry.json lists the sources, whs resolves them, and the result is named full (jsm installed) or open. Cloudflare's skill is pinned by commit and fetched. The run file states the mode, each source with its version, and what was not available. The standard (6.1.1) and the skill say what open loses and what partly substitutes. Acceptance: test/audit.test.mjs shows open with no jsm skill and full with one.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: test/audit.test.mjs shows open with no licensed skill and full with one; whs-run.json records sources, versions and what was not available; standard 6.1.1 and the skill state what open loses.

title: Vision statement (Ryan, 11 Nov) in the README and standard section 1.1
description: Thin wrapper, gaps only, accretive, agents observe and propose, a person approves, production informs the rules. Acceptance: present in README.md and section 1.1 of the standard.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: README.md Vision and standard section 1.1.

title: Standard moved from customer-template and rewritten as draft v5; thin adoption spec left in the template
description: docs/plans/2026-11-11-security-scanning-standard.md. Sections 2 to 14 keep their numbers. Customer-specific content removed. Acceptance: no hit against the confidential term list; the template keeps an archive of v4 and a short adoption spec.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: docs/plans/2026-11-11-security-scanning-standard.md, no hit against the confidential term list; sections 2 to 14 keep their numbers. The template keeps an archive of v4 and a short adoption spec (committed there separately).

title: Audit skill, first form: whs audit prepare, three fragments, skills/workhorse-security-audit
description: prepare requires a repository config, copies one commit out of git without the data paths, runs the deterministic checks over the whole commit and its history as leads (with quoted text removed for findings under a data path), resolves sources and fragments, and writes whs-run.json. The skill binds Cloudflare's process to that surface. Acceptance: test/audit.test.mjs passes. Not yet run on a real target.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: test/audit.test.mjs passes; whs audit prepare ran on one real target in 14 seconds in mode full. A complete audit has not run: that is whs-m6y.3.1.

title: CI confirmed: the suite green on ubuntu-latest and macos-latest, and the reusable gate green on this repository
description: After the first push. If not green, fix and re-run. Acceptance: the run URL and conclusion recorded here.
close_reason: solo: self-verified, not independently reviewed. Evidence: https://github.com/InStrand/workhorse-security/actions/runs/42951014283 on c469ea1: tests ubuntu-latest success, tests macos-latest success, security / security-gate success.

title: Wave 1: the first baseline audit, and the gate in every repository
description: Standard section 12, wave 1.

title: First baseline deep audit on one real repository: the test of the design in standard 6.1
description: Run the audit skill end to end on a real target, profile deep, with a budget the operator sets. The repository config and the record live with the target's owner; nothing about the target enters this pack. Acceptance: a run that ends with both Cloudflare validators passing (or incomplete with its reason); the coverage mode stated; findings as beads in the tracker that belongs to the target. Record here only what is about the pack and holds for any target: whether jsm references worked as reference sections in hunter prompts, what the process needed that the skill did not say, and the number of agent invocations. Proposals for rules, canaries and fragment lines stay on the findings' own beads until each finding is closed (standard 9.6, D15).

comments.author: rgbrgy
comments.text: 11 Nov: whs audit prepare has run on the target at its current main: mode full, three fragments apply, the surface and leads are in a run directory outside every repository. The repository config is a draft made from file names and sizes; the operator confirms the data paths and sets the budget before reconnaissance. The skill is not installed as a skill (the machine's dcg rule refuses hand-made links); use it by path from the checkout.

title: Measure cost before any budget is set
description: Standard 9.4. Reviewer tokens over two weeks of real pull requests; deep-audit agent invocations per run by repository tier; runner minutes; GitHub seats and Secret Protection committers from current billing. A purchase on a customer's organisation is the customer's decision.

title: Gate additions: scheduled history pass, the team's own tests, a hook for the dependency surface check
description: Standard 5.2. The caller workflow gains a weekly schedule that runs whs scan --history. The gate stays one always-run job.

title: Choose Trivy or Checkov and add it as a check with canaries
description: Standard section 4, last row. One registry entry, pinned by SHA-256, with a catching and a quiet case. List its ignore mechanisms and neutralise them.

title: Next Semgrep rules, each with canaries
description: From standard 9.2: a public route with no classified guard; a Convex public mutation with no identity check; a scheduled function with no guard; an unpinned CDN import; a server function that trusts a client-supplied user id. Write a rule only where a pattern is precise enough to gate; the rest become fragment lines.

title: Code owners template: guard files, workflows, agent configuration, security/config.json, the reviewer's instructions, dangerous migration statements
description: Standard 5.4. In a customer's repository this changes their process and is their decision.

title: For each pinned scanner, list every ignore mechanism from its documentation and test that the pack switches it off
description: Today: Semgrep (.semgrepignore replaced, --disable-nosem), zizmor (--no-config, inline ignore comments stripped), gitleaks (--ignore-gitleaks-allow, ignore path, pack config). Not checked from documentation: other Semgrep ignore routes, zizmor's other comment forms, gitleaks baseline files. Add a test per mechanism to test/gate.test.mjs.

title: Runner hardening: Node version check, base-tree result cache, timing on a large repository
description: The gate scans the base tree on every run. Cache findings by commit and registry hash. Measure the gate on the largest repository InStrand works in.

title: Architecture and simplification pass on the runner (independent agent, simplify-and-refactor-code-isomorphically)
description: An independent agent reviews lib/ against the six parts and the skill's method. Known gaps to verify, not assume (standard section 14): the data boundary is applied by the audit preparation and not derived in the surface builder; quoted text is removed after the report is written; the SARIF the pack writes carries raw Semgrep rule ids with a machine path; scanners inherit the whole environment; whs gate cannot take a config kept outside the repository; whs install does not fetch the pinned audit process; range and history are one surface with two selectors; the gitleaks argument list is written three times. Each behaviour change ships with a planted negative. Acceptance: test/run.sh green, canaries green, no weakened test, a report of lines before and after and of every hypothesis the agent rejected.
close_reason: Reviewed by the conductor after an independent agent did the work. Evidence: 13 commits; test/run.sh ends with 0 failures (47 Node tests, 10 canaries, shellcheck) on macOS; the conductor read lib/surface.mjs and lib/scan.mjs in full. Six listed gaps closed, four unlisted defects fixed, each with a planted negative. Linux is unverified until CI runs on the first public push.

title: Command-line ergonomics and whs doctor (independent agent, jsm CLI and doctor skills)
description: An independent agent applies agent-ergonomics-and-intuitiveness-maximization-for-cli-tools and world-class-doctor-mode-for-cli-tools to whs: machine-readable output, help and errors that say what to do next, stable exit codes, and whs doctor (pins installed and verified, Node and Python versions, hooks active, term list present, sources resolved, config valid). Node standard library only. Acceptance: the skill's scorecard before and after, tests for doctor, test/run.sh green.

comments.author: rgbrgy
comments.text: Phase 1 (audit and design) is done by an independent agent: docs/reviews/2026-11-11-cli-audit.md. Score 414 of 1000. Top changes: a crash must exit 2; one command table for parsing, help and suggestions; --json on every command; whs doctor; errors that give the next step, plus whs checks and whs explain. Implementation is parked for the owner's planning round.

title: D14: publish the audit skill as a short trigger in the skills repository; the pack writes the run steps into each run directory
description: whs audit prepare writes PROTOCOL.md into the run directory, composed for the coverage mode that resolved, so the steps always match the code that prepared the run. The installed skill only says: get the pack, run prepare, follow the protocol in the run directory. Then the skill moves to the skills repository and installs with npx skills add.

title: Act on D9: make the pack public or set up vendoring, and prove a call from another repository
description: If public: scan the full history against the confidential term list and with whs scan --history, then change visibility. Then, in a probe repository, call .github/workflows/security.yml at a pinned commit and confirm it runs and which pack commit it used. Verify from GitHub's documentation the access rules for private reusable workflows across organisations (not verified on 11 Nov). Check whether GitHub push protection reacts to the canary fixtures.

comments.author: rgbrgy
comments.text: Learned 11 Nov: GitHub added uses: $/... on 30 July 2026 (same repository at the running commit; needs runner 2.336.0). Probe what $/ resolves to inside a workflow that another repository called. If it is the called repository at the called commit, load the pack through a $/ action and remove the pack-ref input. Also decide whether .ntm/config.toml stays tracked before going public: it holds a local path.

comments.author: rgbrgy
comments.text: Ryan decided public on 11 Nov. Before the change of visibility: the two agent passes land; Ryan answers whether the private commits are replaced by one clean root commit (the early commits hold wording that was later made general, a local path in .ntm/config.toml, and a provenance label on two rules); then the probe call from another repository.

title: D15: private overlay, a second pack root with the same layout, for rules, canaries and fragments that are not public yet
description: whs takes one or more extra roots (checks/semgrep/rules, canaries, fragments). The canary suite covers overlay rules the same way. The overlay lives beside a private record. Standard 9.6.

title: Replayed catalogue surface: apply a repository's migrations to a throwaway Postgres and check the catalogue
description: The accurate form of the Postgres checks. The text rules report comments and do not know that a later migration replaced a definition. Start a local database (the Supabase CLI local stack or a plain Postgres image), apply the migrations in order, then run the Security Advisor lints by SQL and the queries for definers the anonymous role can execute, grants and RLS flags. Deterministic, exact for what the repository says, and needs no production credential. First verify: that a real repository's migrations apply from an empty database; which extensions the image must carry. Deployed state stays a separate surface.

title: Show gate findings in the pull request: job summary and inline annotations from the findings
description: GitHub renders workflow commands as annotations on the changed lines and a Markdown job summary, with no extra tool or token. whs gate writes both when it runs in Actions.

title: D3: whose Anthropic API key runs the CI reviewer (one per customer organisation, spend-limited, is the recommendation)
description: Open since 9 November. Spend is Ryan's decision, and on a customer's organisation the customer's. The advisory reviewer waits on this.

title: One install script that gets everything working (installer-workmanship skill)
description: The owner's requirement of 12 November: a simple script that takes a machine from nothing to a working pack. It checks Node and Python, gets the pack at a pinned commit, runs whs install, puts whs on the path, installs the audit skill, and ends by running whs doctor. An independent agent builds it with the installer-workmanship skill.

title: Audit budget: estimate from the ledger, ceiling and model in the repository config (D17)
description: whs reads a run's coverage ledger and prints the cost of full coverage (units, critics, verifiers) and what a ceiling covers. The repository config holds the ceiling per profile and the model for audit agents. Each run records the agent runs it used. Standard 9.4.

title: Data paths: keep a folder out and let named files back in
description: Today a pattern can only leave files out. Keeping a whole documentation folder out also hides the design documents an audit would use. Add a re-include form that still fails closed: a new file in the folder stays out until it is named.

title: Small defects found in the architecture pass and left open
description: From standard section 14, known gaps on 12 November: an error that is not a usage error exits 1 and should exit 2; the fragments validator checks that some mode needs nothing, not the last; a finding under a data path keeps the tool's message; the reusable workflow has no input for a config kept elsewhere; the gate job fetches the audit process it does not use; the allowlisted environment and the pack-owned git directory are untested on Linux.

title: Audit report: group needs_validation records by the fact that settles them
description: With no sandbox, most records end as needs_validation. Many depend on the same platform fact. The skill should have the coordinator produce one owner checklist: each check once, with the records it settles.

title: Unattended audits need a watcher: approval prompts, usage limits, idle panes
description: A coordinator was stopped for hours by one approval prompt in a subagent. Ship a watcher that costs nothing while it waits and wakes the operator at review points, on a pane exit, on a limit message, or after a set time without change. Add the operator's vetting steps to the skill: validators, ceilings, cited locations, the models actually used, and a re-read of every critical and high finding.

title: Adopt the gate in customer-template: caller workflow and security/config.json
description: Copy workflows/security.yml, pin the pack commit, add the config, make security / security-gate a required check, and remove the template's own gitleaks step once the pack's is shown equal on the same range. init-customer then carries both into clones.

title: Install the gate in a repository InStrand does not own, through fwt, with the config in the engagement repository
description: The customer decides anything that changes its repository or process. Until then the operator runs whs gate locally in the pre-push gate of the overlay.

title: Advisory AI reviewer on pull requests: three-state status, instructions from the base revision, never a required check
description: Standard 5.3. Wraps anthropics/claude-code-security-review as a check of class model with sends_to anthropic, so it reads a surface without the data paths. Instructions are composed from the fragments that apply and read from the base revision. run-every-commit true (the action otherwise caches per pull request); its timeout defaults to 20 minutes; it is not hardened against prompt injection. Status: reviewed with findings, reviewed clean, not reviewed. Needs D3 (whose API key).

title: Deploy wait: the gate on the merged commit, and a preflight that reads check conclusions for that SHA before production is granted
description: Standard 5.5. Deterministic failure stops the deploy; a model's high or critical finding stops it until a named person re-runs with a recorded reason; not reviewed never blocks. Always-run job names with the conditions inside.

title: GitHub posture: baseline file, OpenSSF Scorecard and Allstar
description: Standard section 4. First verify the current Scorecard check list and Allstar policy set, and what organisation security configurations a Free plan allows (all unverified). Scorecard's SARIF goes through the registry as a check that reads a platform surface.

title: Production credentials only in a branch-restricted production environment, proven by a sentinel pull request
description: The first Layer A control. A pull request that edits a workflow to read a production secret must fail to read it. Environments for private repositories need the Team plan (D1). On a customer's organisation this is the customer's decision.

title: Declare posture baselines for Supabase, Cloudflare, Vercel and VPS
description: posture/<platform>.yaml, derived from the threat model per stack. Verify Supabase Management API endpoint names for network restrictions and SSL enforcement first (unverified). Apply and verify steps come with the adapters.

title: Wave 2: adapters, and the audit's findings in SARIF
description: Standard section 12, wave 2.

title: Dependency surface generator, with each advisory route proven in a probe repository
description: Standard 6.3. Lists every dependency declared outside manifests (inline registry or URL imports, CDN script tags, curl piped to a shell, vendored files, container bases, downloaded tools), resolves versions, records the route (lockfile, manifest, submitted graph, SBOM, none). A dependency with route none and no dated exception fails the gate. Known limits: the Advisory Database has no JSR or Deno ecosystem; Dependabot reads Deno dependencies from deno.json and deno.jsonc only; OSV-Scanner has no Deno support. Unverified: whether alerts fire for dependencies sent through the dependency submission API.

title: Experiment: a second-model verifier for the deep audit, measured on canaries
description: Contested in the review of v2 (scores 440 against 620). Decide from the measured detection rate and noise, not from opinion.

title: Customer tier: fixes as patch files from claude-security's suggest-patches job
description: Standard 6.1, for repositories where no agent fixes code through the flywheel.

title: Marker check: stop a run and ask a person when a repository carries material the organisation's rules flag as sensitive
description: Standard 9.1. A config field for the markers and a check that runs before any surface is built for a provider-sending check.

title: Supabase catalogue adapter through a catalogue-only role
description: Standard 6.4. Nightly snapshot: Security Advisor lints by SQL, definers the anonymous role can execute, grants, RLS flags, function body hashes; compared with the last snapshot and with the tree. Its own least-privilege credential, never the deploy token, never an account-wide token in an unattended job.

title: Compare deployed Edge Function sources with the repository
description: From an operator session, weekly. Supabase's function download leaves out import maps and deno.json, so compare sources only.

title: Convex adapter: the production function surface compared for new public functions
description: npx convex function-spec --prod, read-only.

title: Vercel and VPS adapters: public routes, environment separation, deploy identity
description: Standard 6.4.

title: Convert the audit's findings.json to SARIF, and add whs audit publish
description: Standard 6.5 step 1 and section 8. Identity for audit findings: class, symbol or route, and boundary. publish copies the named record files to the config's record directory and nothing else (never the surface or agent scratch).

title: Estate inventory per customer, with tiers and the checks each tier requires
description: Every repository, site, published skill and hand-deployed service. A missing required check becomes a finding: the tier's requirements compared with the checks that ran. Lives in the engagement repository, with the schema here.

title: Move closed findings into the pack as canaries, rules and fragment lines
description: The accretive step, under D15. When a finding is closed, its proposal (kept until then on the finding's bead in the private tracker) moves here in general terms: a canary, a rule where a pattern can catch it, a fragment line. Nothing that says where it came from.

title: Run the jsm static scripts from whs audit prepare in full mode
description: find-fail-open.sh, api-auth-mapper.sh and leak-scan.sh against the surface, their output added to the leads. Today the skill has the agent run them. Never webhook-signature-test.sh; rls-coverage.sql only against a non-production database with a catalogue-only role.

title: Wave 3: the record and the loop
description: Standard section 12, wave 3, and section 8.

title: Evaluate Microsoft's sarif-multitool (match-results-forward) before writing more record code
description: If it matches results across runs as well as the pack's fingerprint comparison, use it. Record the comparison on the same fixtures as test/gate.test.mjs.

title: Daily overdue list by severity and a monthly summary per repository
description: Standard 6.5 step 6.

title: The record: merge a scan into the stored SARIF with baselineState and the states of section 8
description: new, unchanged, updated, absent; triaged, in_progress, verified_closed, accepted_risk. Exploit detail redacted in a repository's own record.

title: The importer: one bead per finding to fix or validate, keyed by fingerprint; an inbox for unattended runs
description: Standard 6.5 step 3. Severity to priority, label security. An unattended run never commits and never creates beads: it writes to Agent Mail or an inbox and the conductor imports.

title: Closure by re-scan: a security bead closes when a later scan of the deployed revision no longer reports its fingerprint
description: Standard 6.5 step 5. Nobody closes a security bead by hand.

title: Triage agent: deduplicate, confirm reachability and severity, mark fix, accept or validate
description: Standard 6.5 step 2. Nothing in needs_validation becomes a fix item without validation.

title: Heartbeat per scheduled job, so a silent job is a finding
description: Standard 9.3. A canary on a schedule: the expected report against the observed one.

title: Probe repositories: advisory routes, cross-repository call, production credential fence
description: probes/README.md.

title: Canaries for model checks: detection rate and noise budget, and the paired injection canary
description: Standard 9.2. A real defect plus text addressed to the reviewer, written at run time from parts. Run on every scanner, rule or model change and monthly.

title: Exploitation check for every confirmed critical or high finding, and log retention guidance
description: A second bead per finding: was it used, which logs would show it, how long are they kept. Guidance for sign-in and session tables to carry IP address and user agent.

title: Wave 4: backfill and drift
description: Standard section 12, wave 4.

title: Backfill the gate and the config across InStrand's repositories
description: workhorse-platform and the customer repositories InStrand owns.

title: flywheel-core add-on registry entry: report drift from the pinned pack and print the install command
description: Check-only. Installed by wh-project-setup into clones and by fwt into repositories InStrand does not own.

title: init-customer carries the caller workflow and the config template into a new clone
description: Standard 9.5.

title: Wave 5: intelligence and scheduled operation
description: Standard section 12, wave 5, and section 7.

title: Zero Wire reader: poll daily, store, parse as data
description: https://radar.cloudflare.com/security/zero-wire/rss. Items carry status, CVE ids and technology tags as categories. The feed holds recent items only, so every poll is stored. The briefing's own AI prompt is never run.

title: Match advisories against each repository's dependency surface: Advisory Database, OSV, vendor advisories, CISA KEV for priority
description: Standard section 7. A match goes to triage; actionable items become beads; the rest are logged with the reason.

title: Scheduled weekly quick audit on InStrand's server, read-only, results to the inbox
description: Standard 6.2 and 6.6. Skipped when nothing changed and the monitors are healthy.

title: D8: set cadence and fix-time targets from the wave 1 cost figures
description: Proposals: weekly quick, monthly deep for active production, quarterly floor; 48 hours, 7 days, 30 days, next quarter. Contested in review: one model held, at 90 percent, that active production systems need a monthly deep audit.

title: Ringed rollout of pack versions with a pinned previous version for rollback
description: Template, one InStrand production repository, one customer pilot, the rest.

title: D5: trial Vercel Security Review beside the standard where a project deploys on Vercel
description: Layers C and D never depend on the host.

title: D2: Renovate for versions, Dependabot for alerts
description: Open. Also unverified: whether Dependabot security updates are free on all plans.
